The install command only touches one folder

A git clone into ~/.claude/skills/TBaguette sits right next to whatever else already lives under ~/.claude/skills/ — other skills, other plugins, things you already trust. It's a fair question whether installing this one could touch any of that. It can't. This page is why, and the actual test that proves it, not a claim restated in different words.

What the command does

The published command checks for an existing clone before doing anything: if ~/.claude/skills/TBaguette/.git already exists, it runs git pull in place; otherwise it runs git clone. The first run installs. Every run after that updates. Neither branch ever reads or writes anywhere else.

Why it can't reach anything else

Both branches are scoped to the single path ~/.claude/skills/TBaguette by construction — a git clone or git pull targeting that path has no mechanism to write outside it. The one case worth naming explicitly is a real collision: something else already sitting at that exact path, that isn't a clone of this repo. git clone refuses outright when its target already exists and is non-empty — it does not merge, does not overwrite, does not ask. It fails loudly and leaves whatever was there exactly as it was. That refusal is git's own behavior, not something this project added on top.

Four scenarios, not one

A single happy-path test would only prove the command works when nothing is in its way, which is the one case nobody actually worried about. The real test runs four scenarios, each against a throwaway HOME directory seeded with fake sibling skills and plugins alongside TBaguette, checksummed before and after:

  • A — fresh install. Nothing at that path yet. Confirms the clone succeeds and the siblings are untouched.
  • B — running it again. Continues from A. Confirms the second run updates in place (git pull) instead of erroring the way a bare git clone would, and that the siblings are still untouched.
  • C — an empty directory already named TBaguette. Confirms git clone is willing to use an empty directory that happens to already exist, and that siblings survive.
  • D — the real collision. A non-empty, non-git directory already sitting at that exact path, with its own unrelated content. Confirms the command refuses rather than merging into it — and that both the colliding directory's own content and every sibling skill survive the refusal.

All twelve checks across those four scenarios pass before this site is ever deployed — plus three more that run the exact command string published above, word for word, through a real shell on any system that has one, rather than trusting that this page's Python reimplementation of it stayed faithful to what actually ships. run_tests.py runs all fifteen alongside everything else, not as a separate manual step someone has to remember.

The test itself

This is scripts/test_install_command.py, unedited — the same file the test suite actually runs, not a representative excerpt.

  1. """Proves the published install command (templates.INSTALL_COMMAND) can never
  2. alter, overwrite, or merge into anything a user already has under
  3. ~/.claude/skills/ that this repo doesn't own — a user asked "won't this alter
  4. other skills?" and this is the actual answer, re-checked on every run rather
  5. than trusted from memory.
  7. Stdlib only, and deliberately not a shell script (this file replaces what was
  8. originally test_install_command.sh): bash is not guaranteed to exist on every
  9. system this might run on, notably Windows without Git Bash or WSL, and even
  10. where a POSIX shell is present, the coreutils it calls out to differ across
  11. platforms in ways that silently break things — the original script's
  12. sha256sum has no equivalent by that name on macOS (it ships shasum -a 256
  13. instead). Python 3 is a much narrower, more realistic requirement here, since
  14. it's already needed to run scripts/generate.py, and git is already required
  15. to install the plugin in the first place — nothing new to ask a reader to
  16. have.
  18. Four scenarios, each in its own throwaway HOME so a real ~/.claude is never
  19. touched:
  20. A. fresh install — clones cleanly
  21. B. re-running once already installed — updates in place (git pull),
  22. does not error
  23. C. an empty dir already named TBaguette — clones into it cleanly
  24. D. a NON-empty, non-git dir already named
  25. TBaguette (the real collision case) — refuses, leaves it untouched
  27. Sibling directories (other skills, other plugins) are populated in every
  28. scenario and checksummed before/after to prove they are never touched, not
  29. just assumed to be.
  31. The install() function below reimplements the published command's logic as
  32. direct git subprocess calls rather than shelling out to run the literal
  33. string — the same two git operations, in the same order, gated by the same
  34. condition, but expressed so this file's core guarantee holds even on a
  35. system with no POSIX shell at all. Where a shell *is* available,
  36. check_matches_published_command() additionally runs the literal string from
  37. templates.INSTALL_COMMAND itself, so the claim "the published command is
  38. safe" stays backed by the actual text shown on the site, not only by code
  39. that is merely intended to match it.
  41. Usage:
  42. python3 scripts/test_install_command.py
  43. """
  45. from __future__ import annotations
  47. import hashlib
  48. import os
  49. import shutil
  50. import subprocess
  51. import sys
  52. import tempfile
  53. from pathlib import Path
  55. sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
  57. from templates import INSTALL_COMMAND # noqa: E402
  59. REPO_URL = "https://github.com/LeSplooch/tbaguette-skills.git"
  61. _checks = 0
  62. _fails = 0
  65. def check(condition: bool, label: str) -> None:
  66. global _checks, _fails
  67. _checks += 1
  68. if condition:
  69. print(f" ok {label}")
  70. else:
  71. print(f" FAIL {label}")
  72. _fails += 1
  75. def install(home: Path) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
  76. """The published install command's logic, as direct git calls instead of
  77. a shell string: if ~/.claude/skills/TBaguette/.git already exists, pull
  78. in place; otherwise clone. Scoped to that single path by construction —
  79. neither branch has any mechanism to read or write anywhere else."""
  80. target = home / ".claude" / "skills" / "TBaguette"
  81. if (target / ".git").is_dir():
  82. return subprocess.run(
  83. ["git", "-C", str(target), "pull"],
  84. capture_output=True, text=True,
  85. )
  86. return subprocess.run(
  87. ["git", "clone", REPO_URL, str(target)],
  88. capture_output=True, text=True,
  89. )
  92. def seed_sibling_skills(home: Path) -> None:
  93. """Fake pre-existing content the install must never touch: a loose
  94. skill directory and a separate plugin, exactly the two shapes
  95. ~/.claude/skills/ actually holds (see orienting-in-unfamiliar-code and
  96. the TBaguette plugin's own layout)."""
  97. other_skill = home / ".claude" / "skills" / "some-other-skill"
  98. other_skill.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
  99. (other_skill / "SKILL.md").write_text(
  100. "precious user content that must survive\n", encoding="utf-8"
  101. )
  103. plugin = home / ".claude" / "skills" / "another-plugin"
  104. (plugin / ".claude-plugin").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
  105. (plugin / ".claude-plugin" / "plugin.json").write_text(
  106. '{"name": "another-plugin"}\n', encoding="utf-8"
  107. )
  108. (plugin / "skills" / "foo").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
  109. (plugin / "skills" / "foo" / "SKILL.md").write_text(
  110. "more precious user content\n", encoding="utf-8"
  111. )
  114. def siblings_checksum(home: Path) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
  115. """(path relative to home, sha256) for every file under the two sibling
  116. directories, sorted — needs no external tool at all, unlike the original
  117. script's `find ... -exec sha256sum {} \\; | sort`, so there is nothing
  118. here that can be missing or spelled differently across platforms."""
  119. roots = (
  120. home / ".claude" / "skills" / "some-other-skill",
  121. home / ".claude" / "skills" / "another-plugin",
  122. )
  123. entries = [
  124. (str(path.relative_to(home)), hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest())
  125. for root in roots
  126. for path in root.rglob("*")
  127. if path.is_file()
  128. ]
  129. return sorted(entries)
  132. def check_matches_published_command(workdir: Path) -> None:
  133. """Best-effort bonus check: on any system with a POSIX shell on PATH,
  134. also runs the literal published command string — not this file's
  135. reimplementation of it — against one fresh scenario. Skipped, not
  136. failed, where no such shell exists (a bare Windows system with neither
  137. Git Bash nor WSL); install() above already proves the same guarantee
  138. there via git directly, which is the whole reason it's written that
  139. way rather than as a wrapper around a shell string."""
  140. shell = shutil.which("bash") or shutil.which("sh")
  141. if shell is None:
  142. print(" (skipped: no POSIX shell on PATH — install() above already "
  143. "verified the same guarantee via git directly, without one)")
  144. return
  146. home = workdir / "shellcheck"
  147. home.mkdir()
  148. seed_sibling_skills(home)
  149. before = siblings_checksum(home)
  151. env = {**os.environ, "HOME": str(home)}
  152. result = subprocess.run(
  153. [shell, "-c", INSTALL_COMMAND], env=env, capture_output=True, text=True,
  154. )
  155. check(result.returncode == 0,
  156. f"the literal published command also exits 0 under {Path(shell).name}")
  157. check((home / ".claude" / "skills" / "TBaguette" / "README.md").is_file(),
  158. "...and actually installs something")
  159. check(before == siblings_checksum(home),
  160. "...without touching the sibling skills, using the exact string "
  161. "published on the site, not a reimplementation of it")
  164. def main() -> int:
  165. workdir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="tbaguette-install-test-"))
  166. try:
  167. print("scenario A: fresh install")
  168. home_a = workdir / "a"
  169. home_a.mkdir()
  170. seed_sibling_skills(home_a)
  171. before_a = siblings_checksum(home_a)
  172. result = install(home_a)
  173. check(result.returncode == 0, "clone exits 0")
  174. check((home_a / ".claude" / "skills" / "TBaguette" / "README.md").is_file(),
  175. "TBaguette content actually present")
  176. check(before_a == siblings_checksum(home_a),
  177. "sibling skills byte-identical after install")
  179. print("scenario B: re-run when already installed (must update, not error)")
  180. home_b = home_a # continues from A, which already installed TBaguette
  181. before_b = siblings_checksum(home_b)
  182. result = install(home_b)
  183. combined_output = (result.stdout or "") + (result.stderr or "")
  184. check(result.returncode == 0, "re-run exits 0 (does not error)")
  185. check(
  186. any(marker in combined_output for marker in
  187. ("Already up to date", "Updating", "Fast-forward")),
  188. "re-run reports a pull, not a clone-refused error",
  189. )
  190. check(before_b == siblings_checksum(home_b),
  191. "sibling skills still byte-identical after re-run")
  193. print("scenario C: an empty pre-existing TBaguette directory")
  194. home_c = workdir / "c"
  195. (home_c / ".claude" / "skills" / "TBaguette").mkdir(parents=True)
  196. seed_sibling_skills(home_c)
  197. before_c = siblings_checksum(home_c)
  198. result = install(home_c)
  199. check(result.returncode == 0, "clone into empty existing dir exits 0")
  200. check((home_c / ".claude" / "skills" / "TBaguette" / "README.md").is_file(),
  201. "TBaguette content actually present")
  202. check(before_c == siblings_checksum(home_c), "sibling skills byte-identical")
  204. print("scenario D: a non-empty, non-git TBaguette directory (real collision)")
  205. home_d = workdir / "d"
  206. target_d = home_d / ".claude" / "skills" / "TBaguette"
  207. target_d.mkdir(parents=True)
  208. marker_file = target_d / "dont-touch-me.txt"
  209. marker_file.write_text(
  210. "unrelated content some other tool put here\n", encoding="utf-8"
  211. )
  212. seed_sibling_skills(home_d)
  213. before_marker = hashlib.sha256(marker_file.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
  214. before_d = siblings_checksum(home_d)
  215. result = install(home_d)
  216. check(result.returncode != 0,
  217. "refuses (nonzero exit) rather than merging into unrelated content")
  218. check(hashlib.sha256(marker_file.read_bytes()).hexdigest() == before_marker,
  219. "the colliding directory's own content is untouched")
  220. check(before_d == siblings_checksum(home_d),
  221. "sibling skills byte-identical even in the refusal case")
  223. print("bonus: the literal published command string, where a shell exists")
  224. check_matches_published_command(workdir)
  225. finally:
  226. shutil.rmtree(workdir, ignore_errors=True)
  228. print()
  229. if _fails == 0:
  230. print(f"{_checks} checks passed.")
  231. return 0
  232. print(f"{_fails} of {_checks} checks FAILED.")
  233. return 1
  236. if __name__ == "__main__":
  237. sys.exit(main())

Run it yourself

Clone the repo and run python3 scripts/test_install_command.py directly, or python3 scripts/run_tests.py for the full suite this page's claims are checked against. Standard-library Python only — no bash required, since it isn't guaranteed to exist on every system this might run on.

La Boulangerie TBaguette is an atelier for Claude Code skills — the judgment calls that sit between the ticket and the commit, organized like a proper bench.
